title: Book 8 — Urania, Chapter 58
paragraphs: This advice strongly commended itself to Themistocles; and without making any reply he went to Eurybiades's ship. Arriving there, he said he wished to communicate a matter that concerned the common good; Eurybiades told him to come on board and speak, if he had anything to say. So Themistocles, sitting down beside him, repeated everything Mnesiphilos had said, as if the ideas were his own, adding many more besides; until at last, by urgent request, he persuaded Eurybiades to come out of his ship and summon the commanders to a council.
